candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reported measurements are treated as geometric means (or another unit/aggregation) changes the effluent concentration inputs used in limit-derivation calculations and thus which numeric limit applies and whether an exceedance is found.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Using one-half the detection limit as a substitute numeric value versus treating the result as non-numeric changes both the applicable limit comparison (Purpose A) and whether the period is classified as having usable data, conditional no-data, or missing evidence (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting sub-MQL nondetects as 'no data' rather than a numeric substitute prevents limit-exceedance comparison for that period (Purpose A) and shifts the case toward documented no-data or unresolved missing-evidence states (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The segment permits two alternative treatments of sub-MQL values; choosing the reported value versus zero changes calculated concentrations and exceedance outcomes (Purpose A) and whether the evidence is treated as a valid numeric result or an ambiguous/missing-data state (Purpose C).

Different interpretations of the instream waste concentration formula or its inputs (F, Qa, Ca, Qe, Ce) yield different derived concentration values, which can change which enforceable numeric limit is selected and whether a reported measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: F    = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F is not fixed in this segment and is defined by reference to external procedures; a different assigned F value changes Cd and therefore the numeric limit deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: The segment allows either 4Q3 or harmonic mean for Qa; selecting one flow statistic over the other changes Cd and can change which numeric discharge limit applies and any exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span: The following formular convert metals reported in total form to dissolved form if criteria are in dissolved form
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether total-reported metal results must be converted to dissolved form before comparison determines which dissolved numeric criteria apply and whether a measurement is treated as enforceable for compliance.
Interpretation of the dissolved-fraction conversion (including TSS source and Kp) changes the converted total-metal criteria used for limit comparison.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TSS is taken from the receiving stream or effluent for intermittent streams changes Kp, C/Ct, and the resulting dissolved numeric limit against which measurements are compared.
This conversion from dissolved criteria (Cr) to total-metal criteria (Ct) directly sets the enforceable numeric limit used when effluent is reported in total form.

The tabulated partition coefficients and derived dissolved values for copper differ between stream and lake rows; applying the wrong row or misreading the coefficients changes the applicable dissolved numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The following formular is used to calculate hardness dependent criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a parameter's limit is treated as hardness-dependent (versus a fixed value) determines which numeric WQC is computed and used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Aluminum (T)                                     Acute                                   e(1.3695[ln(hardness)]+1.8308)                              8061.08346                 If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 750 in cell O113
candidates.computation_change_reason: Acute aluminum limits are normally hardness-derived but are overridden when stream pH is below 6.5; different interpretations of pH applicability or the override value change the enforceable acute limit (Purpose A) and whether missing pH evidence leaves the limit unresolved (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Chronic                                 e(1.3695[ln(hardness)]+0.9161)                              3229.56667                 If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 87 in cell P113
candidates.computation_change_reason: Chronic aluminum limits switch from a hardness-based formula to a fixed value of 87 when stream pH is below 6.5; interpreting pH conditions or available pH evidence differently changes the applicable chronic limit and unresolved missing-evidence classification.
The acute cadmium limit depends on both hardness and the CF1 correction factor; different hardness inputs or CF1 calculations change the resulting numeric limit used for exceedance comparison.
The chronic cadmium limit uses a separate CF2 hardness correction; alternative interpretations of hardness or CF2 change the enforceable chronic numeric limit.
